[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Vantage Data Centers campus is at 45 S Bullard Avenue, Goodyear, Arizona, just outside Phoenix. Per Vantages own current location page (tier-1 operator source, retrieved this session), the 50 acre campus now totals more than one million square feet and 176 MW of critical IT load across five data centers, at an average power density of 250 W per square foot. Two of the five buildings, AZ11 and AZ12, hold Green Globe certification for new construction through the Green Building Initiative. This supersedes an earlier note on this row citing only the original January 2019 announcement figure of 160 MW on 50 acres, the campus has since grown. This registry row represents the overall campus rather than one of the five individually numbered AZ buildings, so the 176 MW total is not applied to this rows critical_it_mw column. This Goodyear, Arizona Vantage campus is distinct from a separate Microsoft campus also located in Goodyear elsewhere in this registry.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Vantage Data Centers facility, TX21, is at Vantages Westover Hills campus in Bexar County, Texas, at the north corner of the crossing of State Highway 151 and Wiseman Boulevard. Local press (San Antonio Report, August 31, 2023, tier-4 source, https://sanantonioreport.org/san-antonio-vantage-data-centers-microsoft-west-side/) reported Vantage purchased this 31 acre parcel on August 9, 2023, noting that Microsoft operates three data centers with over one million square feet of space nearby across Rogers Road, as a neighbor rather than a Vantage tenant. The Baxtel data center directory (tier-5 aggregator, leads-only) independently corroborates the 31 acre figure and states this building became operational in 2025, giving its address as 5207 Rogers Road, San Antonio, TX, matching the DataCenterMap aggregator listing for this same facility. A third aggregator, datacenterHawk, instead lists this facility at 3800 Wiseman Boulevard, San Antonio, TX, conflicting with the other two, this discrepancy between aggregator sources is noted rather than silently resolved. No MW or square footage figure was found published for this facility this session. A prior note on this row associated it with Frontier, a Vantage mega-campus announced August 2025. This is corrected here, Vantages own August 2025 press release (tier-1 operator source, https://vantage-dc.com/news/vantage-data-centers-unveils-plans-for-frontier-a-25b-mega-campus-in-texas-to-meet-unprecedented-ai-demand/) states Frontier is a 1,200 acre, 1.4 GW, 25 billion dollar, ten building campus in Shackelford County, Texas, near Albany, roughly 300 miles from San Antonio and Bexar County. Frontier is not the San Antonio area campus this row belongs to, it is a separate, later, and much larger project elsewhere in Texas.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Vantage Data Centers facility, VA11, is part of Vantages Ashburn I campus in Sterling, Virginia. A prior research pass on this row already recorded that Vantage began planning a 146 MW mega campus in Ashburn in October 2017, completing the first phase in February 2019 with 6 MW of IT capacity as an initial delivery, and that this facility was referenced in 2019 NAIOP and 2020 NVTC regional awards context. Per Vantages own official page for Ashburn I (tier-1 operator source, https://vantage-dc.com/data-center-locations/north-america/ashburn-i-virginia/), this 52 acre campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166, totals 1.7 million square feet at full buildout, over 1 million already operational, and 206 MW of critical IT load, at densities up to 300 W per square foot. The operator describes the campus as eventually housing six multi-story facilities, matching the six VA1-numbered rows (VA11 through VA16) this registry tracks at this campus. Because the 206 MW and 1.7 million sq ft figures are campus-wide totals across all six buildings, not confirmed as this specific buildings own figure, they are not applied to critical_it_mw. VA11 is the specific building named in that 2019 NAIOP and 2020 NVTC awards recognition, though the operators own current page does not break out VA11s individual capacity separate from the six-building campus total.

reading:
Vantage Data Centers launched in 2010 with an investment from Silver Lake Partners and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado. DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake, with Colony Capital, AustralianSuper, GIC, and ADIA cited among its other investors.

The company operates a standardized campus model across three regions, North America, including US operations in Virginia, Arizona, California, Washington, Ohio, and Texas, plus Quebec and Montreal in Canada, EMEA, spanning Germany, Ireland, Italy, Poland, Switzerland, South Africa, and the UK, and APAC, covering Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia, and Taiwan. Vantage's own site highlights a Texas mega-campus described as a $25 billion development with 1.4 gigawatts of capacity under development, one of the larger single-project capacity figures recorded in this registry, comparable in scale to the multi-hundred-megawatt AWS and NTT figures already documented here.

The registry here tracks 13 Vantage facilities across four states, Arizona, California, Texas, and Virginia, a subset of the six US states the operator names on its own site, which additionally lists Washington and Ohio. No aggregate global data center count or total operating MW figure, distinct from the single Texas mega-campus figure, was located in the sources reviewed this session.
